generic_domain.justification: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are a broad and foundational area in deep learning, providing the underlying structure for many models used across various domains. The two given research domains, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL), both use DNNs as their core components to learn and make decisions. MARL involves multiple agents interacting with each other and the environment, while MTRL focuses on enabling a single model to perform multiple tasks efficiently. Both require complex neural architectures provided by DNNs for effective decision-making processes in reinforcement learning. Hence, 'deep neural networks' encompasses these specific research domains by serving as their foundational framework.
